lines.text: But dearest—Did you not understand that I understood?
lines.note: Opens the correspondence's intimate shorthand of mutual understanding.

lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Flush's frantic welcome shows how deeply Elizabeth's attachment to him runs before Italy.

lines.text: By the way, Byron speaks of plucking oranges in his garden at Pisa ...
lines.note: Robert's Pisa memory gives the planned journey a concrete, shared destination.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: Flush's sudden theft jolts the letters into crisis and comedy.

lines.text: Poor Flush—how sorry I am for you, my Ba!
lines.note: Robert answers Elizabeth's alarm with sympathy for Flush.

lines.text: It seems to me that you and I are at one upon the whole question,—only that I am your Flush, and he is mine.
lines.note: Elizabeth's 'I am your Flush, and he is mine' turns the dog dispute into their private joke.

lines.text: If you do go on Monday, our marriage will be impossible for another year—the misery!
lines.note: Robert's urgency about marriage shows the elopement's stakes.

lines.text: Dearest, I write one word, and have one will which is yours.
lines.note: Elizabeth's surrender of will marks the decisive turning point.

lines.text: Words can never tell you, however,—form them, transform them anyway,—how perfectly dear you are to me—perfectly dear to my heart and soul.
lines.note: Robert's retrospective praise crowns their early correspondence.

lines.text: Ever dearest, I write a word that you may read it and know how all is safe so far, and that I am not slain downright with the day—oh, such a day!
lines.note: Elizabeth's first post-wedding letter carries relief and dreamlike disorientation.

lines.text: I feel so as if I had slipped down over the wall into somebody’s garden—I feel ashamed.
lines.note: Elizabeth's garden-wall image captures her post-marriage wonder.

lines.text: Thank you a thousand times for the note, my own Ba.
lines.note: Robert's gratitude answers her wedding-day proof of love.

lines.text: By to-morrow at this time, I shall have you only, to love me—my beloved!
lines.note: The final eve before departure distills everything to 'you only'.

lines.text: Your letters to me I take with me, let the ‘ounces’ cry out aloud, ever so.
lines.note: She cannot leave his letters behind, sealing the archive of their courtship.
